title.narrative: Digital Capabilities for Skills, Resilience and Inclusion

description.narrative: The project’s approach is grounded in the principles of evidence-based planning, inclusive partnership, and system-wide impact. It builds on the Theory of Change that links digital capability development to enhanced skills, resilience, and inclusion across education systems. During the first phase, the project will focus on scoping, stakeholder engagement, and consensus-building, ensuring that design and implementation are informed by national priorities, gender perspectives, and youth participation. The project will be implemented through a multi-stakeholder partnership framework designed to harness the comparative strengths of Commonwealth institutions, national governments, and international partners. The approach emphasises collaboration, policy alignment, and capacity-building, ensuring that interventions are contextually relevant, gender-responsive, and inclusive of youth and small states. The Commonwealth of Learning (COL) will serve as the lead technical partner for open and distance learning (ODL) and technology-enabled education models, contributing expertise in digital pedagogy, content development, and institutional capacity-building. COL will also support the baseline assessment and development of scalable blended learning frameworks. The Commonwealth Tertiary Education Facility (CTEF)—a collaboration between the Ministry of Higher Education, Malaysia, and the Commonwealth Secretariat—will act as a knowledge and policy hub for tertiary education. It will promote innovation, institutional capacity development, and South–South collaboration, ensuring that the project’s priorities translate into tertiary-level and system-wide outcomes. CTEF’s engagement will also strengthen regional knowledge sharing and partnerships among higher education institutions. UN agencies will be engaged to contribute technical expertise in curriculum reform, gender equality, inclusion, and sustainable livelihoods, particularly in addressing gender disparities in access to digital skills and education opportunities for girls and women. The Association of Commonwealth Universities (ACU) will contribute its network and research expertise, supporting data generation, institutional learning, and pilot evaluation across universities and tertiary institutions participating in the initiative. At the national level, the project will support member states and line ministries in policy alignment, local ownership, and integration of digital skills and lifelong learning into national development and labour market strategies. This includes ensuring that small island developing states (SIDS) and small states receive tailored support reflective of their specific connectivity, capacity, and inclusion challenges. To provide strategic oversight and policy alignment, the Commonwealth Education Ministers Action Group (EMAG) will be convened during the scoping phase. EMAG will review findings from the baseline assessment and stakeholder consultations, endorse priority areas for pilot implementation, and guide the transition from existing initiatives toward an integrated framework for digital transformation and youth empowerment.
